fields.summary: Clarify contentReference resolving (esp. in derived profiles)
fields.customfield_10618:
* contentReferences can only be defined in specializations (not constrained), they cannot be changed and always reference the non-constrained definition.

         * contentReferences bring across all the rules that are in the ElementDefinition for the element, including bindings, invariants etc. This should be clarified in the definition of ElementDefinition.contentReference.

         * In another task (e.g. see #13973, #13386) will will define how to constrain the content of a backbone element in a reuseable fashion.

         * Re-using constraints on "normal" typed elements can be done using StructureDefinitions, and even contained StructureDefinitions. This feature is currently under-tested in the reference implementations.

          *Document the consequences of reusing content definitions for resource designers.
fields.description:
I'd like some further clarification concerning how to resolve contentReference.

         See discussion on Zulip:

                     [https://chat.fhir.org/#narrow/stream/conformance/subject/contentReference.20definition]

comments.body:
We have discussed two aspects related to this issue:

         * The definition of ElementDefinition.contentReference says: "Identifies the identity of an element defined elsewhere in the profile whose content rules should be applied to the current element.". What exactly is "content rules", do these include invariants and child constraints?

         * Should we support contained StructureDefinitions, so you could define constraints at type level and refer to these from within the parent structuredefinition

         * We are thinking about removing the notion of contentReference and replace it with a kind of typereference to a contained structuredefinition.

         * If you constrain out an element (setting max cardinality to 0) that is referred to by a contentReference, are elements referring to the constrained out element also constrained out?

         Obviously, there are too many issues around doing this that we need further discussion and consultation.

The proposed changes would apply to R4. Clearly, we cannot redefine this for STU3. However maybe we can clarify the STU3 documentation on correct interpretation and resolving?

         Specifically this part: "Identifies the identity of an element _defined elsewhere in the profile_"

         I think this is incorrect. If we resolve contentreferences from the referencing profile, then nested contentReferences such as Questionnaire.item.item would recursively inherit constraints from parent Questionnaire.item elements (in the same profile!). This leads to all kinds of unexpected issues, as some Forge customers have indeed reported.

         Instead, a contentReference should be resolved from the *defining* profile, i.e. the core resource or datatype profile that introduces the referenced element, similar to how we resolve datatypes. Then we apply the normal inheritance rules; the derived profile inherits constraints from associated elements in the base profile. Only core resources and datatypes are allowed to introduce a contentReference target, and core profiles never define constraints on deeper nested levels. This would provide predictable behavior for contentReferences (in STU3).
